IMPERIO - two-PC test (early build)
===================================

These binaries are self-contained (no install, no Visual C++ redistributable
needed). This is a pre-release build: no installer, no code signing yet.
Windows SmartScreen / antivirus may warn about an unknown unsigned program -
that is expected at this stage.

Copy this WHOLE folder to BOTH PCs.

********************  THE EASY WAY: Imperio.exe on both PCs  **************

  Double-click  Imperio.exe  on BOTH computers. One window, like AnyDesk:

    Left  "This computer"    - this PC's Device ID, its Access Code and the
                               address to type on the other PC. Sharing is
                               on as soon as the window opens.
    Right "Connect to..."    - type the OTHER PC's address (the 100.x
                               Tailscale one, or 192.168.x) and its code,
                               click Connect. The remote screen opens in its
                               own window (F11 = full screen).

  First time on the PC you want to control: click "Allow through firewall..."
  at the bottom and accept the admin prompt (opens UDP 7700).

  Switches on the left: pause sharing, ask before each session (a Yes/No
  dialog appears when someone connects), open mode for your own Tailscale
  devices (no code needed; other networks refused).

  Saved computers: anything you connect to appears as a tile for one-click
  reconnects (right-click a tile to remove it).

  Sharing settings tab: pause sharing, ask before someone connects, record
  sessions (MP4 in Videos\Imperio - also Session > Start recording in the
  remote-screen window), your plan (Free / Pro licence key), and updates
  (checked at start; "Download and install" replaces the exe and restarts).
  Advanced (folded): Tailscale open mode, firewall helper, trust a changed
  identity.

  Closing the window keeps sharing on; Imperio stays in the tray (bottom
  right). Quit from the tray menu.

  Command line still works:  Imperio.exe host [...]  /  Imperio.exe view ...
  The older 1-START-HOST.bat / 2-START-VIEWER.bat launchers still work too.
***************************************************************************

------------------------------------------------------------------------
CASE A: both PCs on the SAME network (same Wi-Fi / router) - EASIEST
------------------------------------------------------------------------

ON THE HOST PC (the one to control):
  1. Right-click  allow-firewall.bat  ->  Run as administrator  (one time).
  2. Open a terminal (PowerShell) in this folder and run:
         .\imperio-host.exe
     It prints something like:
         Device ID : 123 456 789
         Code      : 42 42 42            <-- you'll type this on the viewer
         Direct mode: viewers connect to this machine's IP, udp/7700
     Leave it running. Note the Code.
  3. Find this PC's network IP (run in the same terminal):
         ipconfig | findstr IPv4
     Use the 192.168.x.x or 10.x.x.x address.
     (On the PC this build came from it was 192.168.1.17 - yours may differ.)

ON THE VIEWER PC (the one you use):
  4. Open a terminal in this folder and run (replace IP and code):
         .\imperio-viewer.exe 192.168.1.17 --code 424242
     A window opens showing the host's screen. Move the mouse / type - it
     drives the host. Close the window to end.

  Tips:
    - View only (don't send mouse/keyboard):  add  --no-input
    - If the host has 2+ monitors, switch with  Ctrl+Shift+1 , Ctrl+Shift+2 ...
    - The window title shows fps / round-trip time / latency.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
CASE B: the two PCs are on DIFFERENT networks (over the internet)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
This needs the little rendezvous server (imperio-signal.exe) running somewhere
BOTH PCs can reach - e.g. on the host's network with UDP 7800 port-forwarded
on the router, or on a cheap VPS. Then:

  On the server machine:   .\imperio-signal.exe
  On the host PC:          .\imperio-host.exe --server SERVER_IP:7800
  On the viewer PC:        .\imperio-viewer.exe --id 123456789 --server SERVER_IP:7800 --code 424242
                           (--id is the host's Device ID; spaces optional)

If a direct path can't be punched through the NATs it falls back to relaying
through the server automatically. Start with Case A first.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
UNATTENDED ACCESS (connect without someone reading you a code)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
  On the host, set a permanent password:
         .\imperio-host.exe --password mysecret
  Then the viewer uses  --code mysecret  (it's the password).
  Optional extra security: a TOTP 2nd factor and an "approve each connection"
  prompt can be enabled in C:\ProgramData\Imperio\config.toml.

The first time a viewer connects it records the host's identity key. If you
later see "HOST IDENTITY CHANGED" it means a different machine answered for
that Device ID - stop and check, or pass --trust-new if you expected it.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
WHAT TO WATCH / REPORT BACK
------------------------------------------------------------------------
  - Did the viewer window show the host's screen? Smooth?
  - Did mouse + keyboard work? Any wrong keys (special chars, shortcuts)?
  - Latency: the viewer title shows "rtt" (network round-trip) and "present"
    (capture->display) in ms. Lower is better.
  - Try a UAC prompt on the host (right-click something -> Run as admin): does
    the viewer see it and can you click it? (This only works fully once the
    service is installed as admin - not required for a first test.)
  - Any crashes, freezes, or error lines in either terminal.
